title: Unramifiedness at a point detected by the relative cotangent fibre
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $x\in X$. Write $\Omega^1_{X/Y}$ for the relative differential sheaf [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ for the local ring at $x$, and $\kappa(x)=\mathcal O_{X,x}/\mathfrak m_x$ for its residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. Then the following conditions are equivalent:
(1) there is an open neighbourhood $W\subseteq X$ of $x$ such that $f|_W:W\to Y$ is unramified [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-unramified-morphism];
(2) $\Omega^1_{X/Y,x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\kappa(x)=0$, where the tensor product is module base change [def-weil-module-base-change].
The point $x$ need not be closed, the residue fields need not be equal or perfect, and no Noetherian or flatness assumption is made.

proof.text: Put $F=\Omega^1_{X/Y}$. By [lem-trf-relative-differential-sheaf-base-change], $F$ is quasi-coherent and of finite type. Using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], choose affine neighbourhoods $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $f(x)$ with $f(U)\subset V$ and $A$ finitely generated over $R$. Write $\mathfrak p$ for the prime of $x$ in $U$. By [lem-sc-relative-differentials-affine-sections] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed], $M=F(U)\cong\Omega_{A/R}$ is a finite $A$-module and $F_x\cong M_{\mathfrak p}$. If $m_1,\ldots,m_n$ generate $M$, their images $m_i/1$ generate $M_{\mathfrak p}$ over $A_{\mathfrak p}=\mathcal O_{X,x}$: divide any expression for a numerator by its denominator. Thus $F_x$ is finite over its local ring.

source.place: Tag 02GF (lemma-unramified-at-point), finite-type differential argument; Tags 01V2, 01UT and 056I/056J

proof.text: Assume (1). The affine-cover characterization in [def-weil-unramified-morphism], applied to $f|_W$, gives an affine open $U_0\subset W$ containing $x$ mapping to an affine $V_0\subset Y$, with coordinate ring map of finite type and $\Omega_{\mathcal O_X(U_0)/\mathcal O_Y(V_0)}=0$. This is also an affine chart for the original morphism $f$. By [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], $F|_{U_0}$ is the sheaf associated to this zero module, hence zero. In particular $F_x=0$, and tensoring the zero module with $\kappa(x)$ gives (2).

source.place: Tag 02GF, implication (1) to (3) and (5); Tag 02G4 affine definition and Tag 01UT

proof.text: Assume (2). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] to the finite $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module $F_x$ from Step 1, taking the generating family to be empty. Over the commutative ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, the balanced maps $m\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes m$ and $a\otimes m\mapsto m\otimes a$ are inverse linear maps: their composites fix every pure tensor, and pure tensors generate. Thus (2) makes $\kappa(x)\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}F_x$ zero. It is generated by the empty family, so the cited tensor formulation of Nakayama says the empty family generates $F_x$. Therefore $F_x=0$.

source.place: Tag 02GF, equivalence of (3) and (5), invoking Algebra Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK)

proof.text: Return to $U,A,M,\mathfrak p$ of Step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed], $F_x=0$ means $\operatorname{Ann}_A(M)\not\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Choose $g\in\operatorname{Ann}_A(M)\setminus\mathfrak p$. Then $gM=0$ and $M_g=0$: every fraction satisfies $m/g^r=(gm)/g^{r+1}=0$. Since $M\cong\Omega_{A/R}$, [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization], with multiplicative subset $\{1,g,g^2,\ldots\}\subset A$, gives $\Omega_{A_g/R}\cong M_g=0$.

source.place: Tag 02GF, support argument for (3) to (1), in the affine-annihilator form of Tags 056I/056J; Algebra Tag 00RT

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], $D(g)\subset U$ is an affine open containing $x$ with coordinate ring $A_g$. If $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ generate $A$ over $R$, then $a_1/1,\ldots,a_n/1,1/g$ generate $A_g$ over $R$, since every fraction is a polynomial in these elements. Step 4 therefore supplies a finite-type affine chart $D(g)=\operatorname{Spec}A_g\to V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with zero relative differentials. The affine-cover characterization of [def-weil-unramified-morphism] makes $f|_{D(g)}:D(g)\to Y$ unramified. Taking $W=D(g)$ proves (1).

source.place: Tag 02GF, affine version of (3) to (1); Tags 02G4/02G6 and Schemes Tags 01I3/01HV

proof_origin.place: Tag 02GF (lemma-unramified-at-point), equivalence (1) with (5): finite generation, Nakayama, and the affine-annihilator version of the support argument; Tags 056I/056J and Algebra 00RT.
